# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination: a directory path, an rsync:// or scp-style host:path, or a
# mount. Can be overridden by setting the BACKUP_DEST env var.
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-/work/backups}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

# Fail loudly if the source is missing or the destination isn't set.
[ -d logs ] || { echo "error: no logs/ directory here" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "$DEST" ] || { echo "error: backup destination not set (BACKUP_DEST)" >&2; exit 1; }

# Copy the tarball into a directory that already exists on the destination.
mkdir -p "$DEST"
cp -p "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"

echo "wrote $BUNDLE -> $DEST/$BUNDLE"

#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

# Backup destination: a directory path, a mount, or an scp-style host:path.
# Can be overridden by setting the BACKUP_DEST env var.
DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-/work/backups}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

# Fail loudly if the source is missing or the destination isn't set.
[ -d logs ] || { echo "error: no logs/ directory here" >&2; exit 1; }
[ -n "$DEST" ] || { echo "error: backup destination not set (BACKUP_DEST)" >&2; exit 1; }

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/

# Destination may be a local dir (cp) or host:path (scp).
case "$DEST" in
	*:*)
		scp -p "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
		;;
	*)
		mkdir -p "$DEST"
		cp -p "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
		;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE -> $DEST/$BUNDLE"
